items.title: PANW Q1 Earnings Beat Estimates on Broad-Based Security Growth
items.summary: Palo Alto Networks (PANW) reported Q1 fiscal 2027 earnings of $1.05 per share, beating estimates by 8.3%, with revenues surging 39.2% to $3.445 billion. Next-Generation Security ARR jumped 66% to $9.73 billion, driven by 170 net new platformizations and strong security demand. The company raised its fiscal 2027 revenue outlook to $14.52-$14.57 billion and EPS guidance to $4.26-$4.30.

items.title: PANW Q1 Earnings Call Highlights $4.5 Billion AI Deal and Outlook
items.summary: Palo Alto Networks (PANW) raised its fiscal 2027 revenue guidance to $14.52B-$14.57B and adjusted EPS to $4.26-$4.30, driven by strong demand across all segments. The company announced a $4.5B all-stock acquisition of Applied Compute to develop AI model training capabilities for enterprise customers, targeting $1B in security ARR by FY29. While the deal will pressure margins near-term (100-200 basis points reduction in FY27-28), PANW recorded 170 net new platform adoptions and 53% Cortex revenue growth.

items.title: Oracle vs. Palo Alto Networks: Which Tech Stock Is the Better Buy in 2026?
items.summary: The article compares Oracle and Palo Alto Networks as enterprise tech investments for 2026. Oracle, with 22% revenue growth and strong cloud infrastructure demand, trades at a forward P/E of 15x with expected 23% earnings growth. Palo Alto Networks shows 25% revenue growth but trades at a steep 94x forward P/E multiple. The author recommends Oracle due to superior earnings growth potential, massive contracted revenue backlog ($664B), and more attractive valuation, despite risks from AI demand fluctuations and high leverage.

items.title: Why Palo Alto Networks Stock Jumped 15% In August Before Falling This Week
items.summary: Palo Alto Networks stock surged 15% in August driven by strong demand for cybersecurity solutions amid AI threats, but fell over 10% this week after reporting Q4 earnings with disappointing fiscal 2027 guidance of 23-24% revenue growth. The stock trades at a premium P/S ratio of 22x, requiring investors to believe in sustained 20%+ growth and significant margin expansion to justify current valuations.

items.title: Palo Alto Networks Is Worth Nearly $300 Billion. A Year Ago It Was Worth About $113 Billion.
items.summary: Palo Alto Networks' market value nearly tripled in a year from $113 billion to $295 billion, but the underlying business growth doesn't justify the valuation increase. While the company showed solid Q3 results with 31% revenue growth and strong next-generation security ARR growth of 60%, much of this came from acquisitions. The stock now trades at 96x forward earnings, pricing in years of excellent execution with limited margin of safety.
